new_statements.quote: [Perrin 2019 §1.3.1] « La langue basari compte 2 registres : bas (non noté) et haut (noté ´). Ils sont attestés par les paires suivantes : afən 'percer', 'émerger' / afə́n 'lire', 'compter' ; afan 'semer à la volée' / afán 'vendre' ; ɐfulí 'bavarder' / ɐfúlí 'moisir' ... » [Kane 2020 p. 36] « Lorsque le mot ne compte que des voyelles faibles (ə, a, ɛ), il est caractérisé par une suite de syllables non intenses. » [p. 41] « Nous constatons que l'oniyan est une langue à ton puisqu'il y a des oppositions au niveau des paires minimales qui se distinguent de par le ton. »
new_statements.translation: [Perrin] 'Basari has 2 tone registers: low (unmarked) and high (marked with an acute). They are attested by the following pairs: afən 'pierce, emerge' / afə́n 'read, count'; afan 'broadcast-sow' / afán 'sell'; ɐfulí 'chat' / ɐfúlí 'go mouldy' ...' [Kane p. 36] 'When the word contains only weak vowels (ə, a, ɛ), it is characterised by a sequence of non-intense syllables.' [p. 41] 'We observe that Oniyan is a tone language, since there are minimal-pair oppositions distinguished by tone.'

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Copies checked (1) Perrin 2019: line 614 = OpenEdition par. 55, sec. 1.3.1 'Presentation du systeme': 'La langue basari compte 2 registres : bas (non note) et haut (note ́). Ils sont attestes par les paires suivantes : 32. afən 'percer', 'emerger'/afə́n 'lire', 'compter'; afan 'semer a la volee'/afán 'vendre'; ɐfulí 'bavarder'/ɐfúlí 'moisir'; fɛ 'ou ?'/fɛ́ 'quel(les)'' -- verbatim as quoted (same passage in HAL preprint l.1116, printed p. 28, diacritics stripped by extracted text there). I read par. 55-75 (1.3 tone system: floating H, downdrift, HL contours word-internally and at phrase edges, tone fusion, grammatical/polar tone; 1.4 syllable structure): no sentence on word stress, accent o…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Both accessible modern descriptions analyse Oniyan as a two-level (H/L) tone language with downstep/downdrift and contour realisations; neither states a position for word stress or discusses accent. Kane's lone remark that words with only 'weak' vowels (ə, a, ɛ) have no 'intense' syllable echoes the Tenda 'strong/weak vowel' accent framework (Santos for Konyagi: weak vowels cannot bear the root-initial word accent) but gives no placement rule for Oniyan.
new_statements.exceptions: None (no stress rule stated). Tonal particulars: floating H after some roots, HL contour before pause, downdrift after H-L, polarity tone on suffix -ɛ.
new_statements.domain_note: Tone described on isolated words and within phrases (Perrin §1.3.2.3 phrase-initial/final modulations). A dedicated stress section exists only in Winters & Winters 2002 §3.0 'Accent tonique' pp. 32-34, which could not be opened.
new_statements.identity_note: All opened sources describe Oniyan/Basari of Senegal-Guinea (bass1258): Perrin 2019 fieldwork mainly Ethiès/Salémata area (Senegal); Winters & Winters 2004 explicitly the Ane dialect (hills south of Kédougou), other dialects Këɗ (Guinea) and Oxalac; Kane 2020 Senegalese Oniyan. Caution: Glottolog's bass1258 bibliography (as passed in glottolog_refs) is contaminated with works on the unrelated Gur language Ntcham, also called 'Bassari/Bassar' of Togo-Ghana (ntch1242): Cox 1974 'La phonologie du bassari', Cox 1971, 1986, 2003, Crunden 1984, Bearth 2000, B'Nantim 1994 — these must not be used for bass1258.

sources.note: Ch. 2 §2.6 'La tonologie' pp. 36-40: four surface tones (H, L, downstepped H, falling HL), two underlying level tones, tonal minimal pairs; p. 41 summary 'l'oniyan est une langue à ton'. Only prominence-related remark (p. 36): a word containing only weak vowels (ə, a, ɛ) 'est caractérisé par une suite de syllables non intenses'. No statement of stress position; tones not marked after ch. 2.
